findings.text: `describe` is on the read allowlist (worker_git_shim.py:72) and this line forwards it with GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0, but on git 2.39.3 `git describe --dirty` refreshes and writes the target checkout's index in-process; measured on a fresh fixture with a backwards-stale stat cache, the index sha moved fbd5200a->3f634244 through the reviewed shim, both direct controls moved it (OPT_LOCKS=0 and OPT_LOCKS=1 with no shim), no child process was spawned (GIT_TRACE), and a second call left it unchanged — the same artifact the fix closes for `status`, and the same class as escape 2, so an allowlisted read still writes another checkout under the instrument the fix chose; `describe` without --dirty left the index unchanged.

item_verdicts.diff: the diff adds the resolve step, the output-option refusal (worker_git_shim.py:302) and the GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 forwarding (worker_git_shim.py:605), each hunks'-worth tested; I confirmed each closure by red-at-head measurement (deleting the hunk restores the escape) but found one allowlisted read the second hunk does not cover.
item_verdicts.done_when: the change's gate holds where the run claimed it: I re-measured the two closures independently rather than trusting the manifest — all eight escape-1 forms refuse at head and the mutated-shim control forwards them (writing its 13-byte file, the positive control that the instrument sees writes), and the escape-2 case is carried by the index measurement at tests/test_git_shim_checks_the_resolved_repo.py:528's condition.
item_verdicts.goal: Read the plan section and the reviewed run's manifest, then drove the shim at head ab38cee8 against a synthetic other checkout in /tmp: the resolve-then-compare step now refuses a mutating verb aimed elsewhere (reset --hard and commit both exit 97) and refuses an output option carried by a forwarded read (--output, joined and separated; --output-directory; a home-directed path; all exit 97 with no file added), so both escapes the prior review measured are closed for the forms measured — with one same-class forwarded write still open (see FINDING), which the goal's own probing clause asks for.
item_verdicts.manifest: the reviewed run has exited (attempt 5, exit 0) with status complete and a clean worktree at ab38cee8b61555edc015c54afe7211d2c043c99a, equal to the review fence's keyed head, so this review read a settled tree and the prior review's premise was verified at its own head (git show a370c5be:reckon/worker_git_shim.py carries neither hunk).
item_verdicts.write_paths: the head diff 7f97afda..ab38cee8 touches reckon/worker_git_shim.py, reckon/worker_shims/git, reckon/crew/dispatch.py, tests/test_git_shim_checks_the_resolved_repo.py, tests/test_worker_path_carries_shims.py and the plan's own evidence and figures — the set the run declared, with no adjacent cleanup.

justifications.durability: the assertions read observable artifacts (index bytes and exit status) rather than internals, and the index test derives its staleness from the fixture's own stat so it does not decay with the calendar.
justifications.evidence: each hunk carries a targeted test (tests/test_git_shim_checks_the_resolved_repo.py:528 builds the exact condition under which the write occurs — a stat cache stale backwards — which I validated separately by driving direct git on the same fixture), so the tests measure the escapes and not a proxy; the second hunk's coverage gap is the one path no test exercises.
justifications.fit: the refusal reuses the module's existing resolve-then-compare shape and its REFUSAL_STATUS constant (worker_git_shim.py:593 _forward), extending the guard it repairs rather than adding a parallel mechanism.
justifications.goal_fidelity: all --output forms exit 97 at head while the mutated shim forwards them (exit 0, file written), and the status refresh leaves the index unchanged at head where the mutated shim moves it — for the class the plan names, the closure holds; the FINDING below shows the same class is not closed for every allowlisted read.
justifications.scope_discipline: the diff is the module, its entry script, dispatch.py's PATH provisioning, two test files and the plan's own evidence/figures, matching the run's declared changed_paths with nothing outside that set.
